sentences.text:
Author: Rajesh Bindal
Bench: Rajesh Bindal
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. /2025

Sakram @ Sangram Appellan
 Versus
 State Of Rajasthan Resp
 O R D E R
Leave granted.
The appellant has been charged for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376 & 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 3 and 4 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and 3(2)(V) of the SC/ST Act.
We have been informed that the trial has already begun and only 10 out of 28 witnesses have been examined.
Most of the remaining witnesses would be the police witnesses.
We have also taken note of the period of incarceration of the appellant which is stated to be around 1 year and 3 months.
Considering the above, we are inclined to set aside the impugned order and grant bail to the appellant.
Accordingly, the impugned order stands set aside and the appellant is granted bail on terms and conditions which are to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
The appeal stands allowed accordingly.
